owner_system: NotebookLM (Google), an external vendor product outside this repo and outside suengj-com.

surface_decides: internal rendering of the audio overview or notebook UX it generates
voice and pacing of its generated audio, within what the supplied source material supports
core_decides: all editorial content, claim selection, and verification — NotebookLM never adds a fact

constraints.input_format: accepts uploaded text/PDF as notebook sources; does not accept this repo's schemas directly
constraints.output_control: no control over the vendor's generated script phrasing beyond the source content and framing supplied
constraints.editorial_authority: none — see docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §7, 'NotebookLM is an adapter and may never become editorial authority or a runtime dependency'

publication_boundary: NotebookLM never marks anything published; it is not a publication surface and holds no publication authority at all.

replaceable.note: NotebookLM is an adapter, not editorial authority (docs/architecture/V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §7, and stop condition §9 item 8), and may be swapped for another notebook/audio-overview vendor without a Core change.

notes.artifact_vocabulary: NotebookLM markets this as an 'audio overview'. That is a vendor product name, not our artifact vocabulary; its editorial shape is a two-host dialogue, so it maps to audio/dialogue. Naming it after the vendor would let an adapter's branding leak into Core semantics.
